REPORT

Subject Further to "SECRET INFORMATION". Brothel at No. 108 and 650
Weihaiwei Road. Submitted April 14th, 1939.
Made by Sub-Inspt. Varndell. Forwarded by （签名）

Sir,

With reference to the above, I respectfully beg to
submit further information on the subject.

On the 28/4/39, D.I. Tabrum attached to Bubbling
Well Station telephoned the undersigned stating, that a Russian
named, Alexander Geller, who gave his residence as, No. 650
Weihaiwei Road, reported to him through D.S.I. Goloobkoff, that
one of three Korean prostitutes of the above address is suffering
from Venereal Disease of the throat, Geller stating, that this
girl had requested him to help her be freed from prostitution,
therefore under the circumstances, he reported the matter.

D.I. Tabrum requested information, if any, concerning
the type of premise, the undersigned duly informed him that
this particular house was under investigation, therefore Geller
was referred to the undersigned who has completed investigations.

Subject U.S. Marine and Naval Personnel Registered in Foreign Lodging Houses
During May 1939.

Made by. D.S. Mischenko Forwarded by Inspector (签名)

I beg to forward herewith revised list of
U.S. Marine and Naval Personnel residing in foreign
lodging houses in the International Settlement during
May 1939.

The information contained in the revised list
was obtained by the undersigned and C.D.S. 24, Hsu Cheh
Hsin, after lengthy and discreet enquiries had been made
among the house-keepers, as well as by questioning of
the Chinese servants in their employment, and by means
of obtaining additional lodging house registration slips
of the persons concerned.

(手写符号)

In view of the delicate nature of the enquiry,
great discretion was exercised in order not to hurt the
feelings of the people concerned, or to arouse unnecessary
suspicion. The enquiry was rendered the more difficult
by frequent changes which occur in the relationship and
residence between the girls and the U.S. Naval and
Marine Personnel.

In addition to giving particulars of the name,
age, branch of service, date of registration of the
U.S. Naval and Marine Personnel concerned, the revised
list gives the name, nationality and other details of
each female person with whom the Personnel is occupying
room in so far as such particulars ascertained in the
course of this enquiry.

Copy prepared together
with list sent Major Madden.

Subject. Porter D. DILLEY, American Newsreel cameraman

Made by. D.S. Fitts Forwarded by. C. Crawford

Porter D. DILLEY, American, about 35-40
years of age, is according to enquiries, a newsreel
cameraman who wanders from time to time to various
parts of the globe securing pictures of travel and
scenic interest to be made up into what are commonly
known as screen travelogues. When he has obtained
sufficient material he returns to the United States
where he moves from town to town giving lectures on
the various phases of life in foreign lands which he
has visited, utilizing, of course, his films.

He has no connection with any Hollywood Studio
or any American publication. He is said to make a
fair living from this type of business which he has
followed for years.

Prior to arriving in Shanghai on January 19,
1939 in the s.s. "President Pierce" from Kobe, he
spent three to four months in Japan taking moving
pictures with the permission of the Japanese Government.
In this connection it is believed he was subsidized to
a certain extent by the Japanese Authorities to secure
films of the country having a big interest for the
American public. In Japan his address was Dai Ito
Hotel, Tokyo.

While in Shanghai he resided at the Navy
Y.M.C.A., Szechuen Road, but made very few friends
here.

撰写人. D.S. Fitts 转呈人. C. Crawford

Porter D. DILLEY，美国人，约35-40
岁，据调查，他是一名新闻片
摄影师，不时前往全球各地
拍摄具有旅行和风景趣味的影片，
并将其制作成通常被称为银幕旅行游记的片子。
当他获得足够的素材后，便返回美国，
在那里辗转于各个城镇，利用其影片
就其所访异国生活的各个方面进行演讲。

他与任何好莱坞制片厂
或任何美国出版物均无关联。据说他
靠这种已从事多年的业务维持着
相当不错的生活。

在1939年1月19日乘坐“皮尔斯总统”号轮船
从神户抵达上海之前，他在日本度过了
三到四个月，经日本政府许可拍摄
电影。在此方面，据信他得到日本当局
一定程度的资助，以获取对美国公众
具有重大兴趣的国家影片。在日本期间，
他的地址是东京大伊藤酒店。

在上海期间，他居住在四川路
海军青年会，但在此地结交的朋友
很少。

taking pictures on Chapoo Road Bridge, but was
released shortly afterwards, when he made it known
that he had secured permission from Captain NISHIHARA,
Naval Spokesman at the Press Conference to take
pictures in the area north of Soochow Creek.

DILLEY left Shanghai for Manila in the s.s.

he is expected to return in a leisurely fashion to
America for the purpose of giving another series of
lectures.

His home address is reported as being :-
c/o 827-P - P. Street,
Bakerfield,
California.

Careful investigations made by this office
have shown that DILLEY has never had any connections
with Room 405, 210 Kiukiang Road, which is the office
of the "Alexander Publishing and Printing Company,"
the sole proprietor of which is a young American of
radical tendencies named Alexander Hassler BUCHMAN.
As far as can be ascertained DILLEY has never met

DEC 5 1930
U. S. Sailors' Transfers Are
Objected By Wives
Japanese Women Protest Against Navy Husbands
Being Sent Home, Leaving Them Behind
Without Chance Of Going To States
Modern "Mme. Butterflies" in Shanghai are up in arms over the short-term transfers of their "Captain Pinkertons."
If the U.S. Navy Department does not heed the appeals of Japanese wives of American sailors and stop transferring them before the expiration of their periods of service in China, a series of blasted romances such as the one described in Puccini's famed opera may be witnessed in Shanghai, it was indicated in an article appearing in the Japanese daily "Mainichi" yesterday.
Japanese wives of American "Gobs" are launching a campaign to voice a concerted protest against the action of the American naval authorities which threatens to deprive them of their mates, the paper said.
There are quite a number of Japanese girls in Shanghai who have become the common law wives of American sailors, the journal stated. The girls say the recent orders of the American naval authorities regarding transfers of sailors appear to be directed against those who have Japanese wives here, according to the "Mainichi."
Naval Regulations
American naval regulations usually allow sailors to remain in the Orient for a period of two years, which can be renewed on request, the paper said.
In spite of this customary procedure, many sailors in Shanghai have been transferred one by one since last month, the journal stated.
Several groups of Japanese wives are meeting to have heart to heart talks on ways and means to save their romances from being shipwrecked, according to the daily.
"The American Navy is transferring our husbands just because they are married to Japanese girls," a spokesman for the discontented wives told a reporter of the "Mainichi" at a conference on Saturday.
"Some of us have been married four years and have children. Formerly our husbands could prolong their stay here if they asked for permission after two years of service time here.
"But now since last month, some of the men with Japanese wives have been ordered to leave before their two-year terms were up.
"We simply can't understand this because things have changed so suddenly and our husbands' requests to get their service time here extended have been turned down by the Navy officials.
"This Is A Cruel Thing"
"This is a cruel thing to do to us, and they seem to be making these orders only for the sailors who are with Japanese girls.
"Our husbands' chums who are with girls of other nationalities are staying right here when they want to. The sailors who are married to Chinese girls are not affected by these new transfer orders.
"We can't understand it. It looks to us as if it was done deliberately by the American Navy officials."
A group of Japanese wives met at a tea room on Bubbling Well Road on Saturday to air their grievances. Their names were given by the journal as Mrs. Clara Uyehara, Mrs. Margaret Oki, Mrs. Nola Nakata and Mrs. Catherine Oshima.
Even if they are married according to the laws of the United States, they cannot go to America with their husbands because of immigration restrictions, the paper pointed out.

1930年12月5日
美国水兵调动遭妻子反对
日本女性抗议海军丈夫被遣返，将其抛下且无机会前往美国
上海的现代“蝴蝶夫人”们因她们的“平克顿船长”们的短期调动而群情激愤。
据昨日日本日报《每日新闻》刊登的一篇文章指出，如果美国海军部不听从美国水兵的日本籍妻子的呼吁，停止在其在华服役期满前进行调动，上海可能会上演一系列如普契尼著名歌剧中所描述的那般破碎的浪漫故事。
该报称，美国“大兵”的日本籍妻子们正在发起一场运动，以共同抗议美国海军当局威胁剥夺她们伴侣的行动。
该期刊指出，上海有不少日本女孩已成为美国水兵的事实婚姻妻子。据《每日新闻》报道，这些女孩表示，美国海军当局近期关于水兵调动的命令似乎是针对那些在此拥有日本籍妻子的人。
海军条例
该报称，美国海军条例通常允许水兵在东方服役两年，经申请可续期。
该期刊指出，尽管有此惯例，自上个月以来，上海的许多水兵已被逐一调动。
据该日报报道，几群日本籍妻子正在聚会，坦诚交流挽救其浪漫关系免遭破灭的方法与途径。
“美国海军调动我们的丈夫，仅仅因为他们娶了日本女孩，”一位不满的妻子代表在周六的一次会议上对《每日新闻》的记者说。
“我们中有些人已经结婚四年并育有子女。以前，如果我们的丈夫在此服役满两年后申请许可，可以延长停留时间。
“但自从上个月以来，一些拥有日本籍妻子的男子被命令在两年任期未满前离开。
“我们根本无法理解这一点，因为情况变化如此突然，而我们丈夫延长在此服役时间的请求均被海军官员驳回。
“这是残酷的行为”
“这对我们来说是一种残酷的行为，而且他们似乎只针对与日本女孩在一起的水兵发布这些命令。
“我们丈夫那些与其他国籍女孩在一起的伙伴，只要愿意就可以留在这里。与中国女孩结婚的水兵不受这些新调动令的影响。
“我们无法理解。在我们看来，这似乎是美国海军官员故意为之。”
周六，一群日本籍妻子在静安寺路（Bubbling Well Road）的一家茶室聚会，倾诉她们的不满。该报列出了她们的名字：克拉拉·上原（Clara Uyehara）夫人、玛格丽特·冲（Margaret Oki）夫人、诺拉·中田（Nola Nakata）夫人和凯瑟琳·大岛（Catherine Oshima）夫人。
该报指出，即使她们根据美国法律结婚，由于移民限制，她们也无法随丈夫前往美国。
